### Keyboard and mouse input contract

- Current Windows `GetKeyInfo` never sets a key code, and POSIX `TryConsumeSpecialSequence` discards special keys. Completing input therefore requires actual production decoder changes as well as changing public types.
- Windows: translate `KEY_EVENT_RECORD::wVirtualKeyCode` to `VKEY`, including the corrected bracket names, retain native down/up ordering, and expand repeated key-down records so navigation repeats as well as text. Determine `autoRepeatKeyDown` from the key's held state and repetitions, including repeated records whose count is one. Queue each key-down before its associated native character unit; key-up does not create text. Preserve character units and modifiers in native order, without combining or replacing UTF-16 surrogates in the backend. Use the [Microsoft key-record contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/key-event-record-str).
- POSIX: replace the discard-only path with an incremental decoder for the supported xterm-compatible UTF-8 terminal input. Cover Tab/Shift+Tab, Enter, Backspace, Escape, arrows, Home/End, Insert/Delete, PageUp/PageDown, function keys, and keypad sequences that identify a key. Recognize both CSI and SS3 forms and their modifier parameters. Map ASCII keys where identifiable and use `VKEY::KEY_UNKNOWN` when text has no reliable virtual-key mapping. Preserve the existing `Char` stream independently of key-code translation.
- The baseline POSIX contract reports a logical `KeyDown` followed by `Char` when the input represents text or an existing character control. Ordinary legacy terminal input does not establish physical release timing, held-key repeat state, Caps Lock, or every modifier combination: do not synthesize physical `KeyUp` events or claim such fields are known. Leave unobservable flags false. Resolve ambiguous control bytes in favor of the named terminal control (for example Tab rather than Ctrl+I), and document the supported mappings and limitations. A richer negotiated keyboard protocol is not a prerequisite for the playground. The terminal sequence reference is [XTerm Control Sequences](https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html).
- Preserve incomplete UTF-8, CSI, SS3, and SGR mouse sequences across reads; a read boundary is not an event boundary. Keep Escape disambiguation deadline-driven. Drain already buffered complete input before blocking for another read, including when a consumed unsupported sequence produces no event. Validate parameter counts, numeric overflow, and mouse coordinates before using them. Unsupported complete control sequences must not leak their suffix into typed text; malformed input must resynchronize without losing later valid input or starving timers/resizes.
- `NativeWindowCharInfo::code` remains one native `wchar_t` unit: UTF-16 on Windows and UTF-32 on Linux/macOS. Keep the playground's scalar assembly and invalid-unit resynchronization in the consumer using `vl::encoding::UtfConversion<wchar_t>::To32`; drawing and width measurement remain scalar-based.
- Keep movement, press, release, double-click, and both wheel axes available in the library for all three supported mouse buttons. The left-button-only rule applies to playground actions. Populate current button state consistently; use a signed wheel delta with 120 units per notch, positive vertical for up and positive horizontal for right. Windows uses the signed high word of the native record; see [Microsoft's mouse-record contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/mouse-event-record-str).
- Retain POSIX all-motion/SGR mouse tracking and the current documented double-click convention: a double-click replaces the second down callback. Restore any terminal modes acquired by input handling on normal shutdown and startup/callback failure. Do not add input workers, busy polling, or new cross-thread TUI operations.

### Playground layout, navigation, and history

- There are two persistent pages, Canvas and History, and one transient Shapes menu. Reserve terminal row 0 for ` Canvas `, ` History `, and ` Shapes `, in that order. Use white text, blue selected background, and gray unselected background; use logical RGB `FFFFFF`, `000080`, and `808080` respectively. Shapes is selected while its menu is open, over the previously active page.
- The Canvas border starts on row 1, moving logical paper `(0,0)` to terminal `(1,2)`. The command box stays at the bottom, retains background `404040`, wraps by scalar display width, and grows upward. Cap its height at `max(0, terminalHeight - 1)` so row 0 remains reserved; show the trailing input rows needed to keep its cursor visible. Omit borders/paper when their dimensions are invalid and forbid drag starts without a paper interior. Derive rendering, hit testing, menu bounds, and mouse-to-paper translation from the same current layout.
- TAB cycles Canvas -> History -> Shapes -> Canvas; Shift+TAB reverses the cycle. Clicking Canvas or History activates that page; clicking Shapes opens its menu. Preserve the complete Canvas draft while navigating. History has no editable command box. Small terminals clip the UI and keep keyboard navigation usable; avoid empty-buffer drawing calls and invalid rectangle ranges.
- Handle Tab and arrow navigation in `KeyDown`. Keep text, Enter, Backspace, and Escape controls in `Char`, as in the current consumer. A control with both key and character callbacks must act exactly once, including after a callback changes the active page or menu state. Do not insert Tab into the draft.
- Keep one durable record per accepted painting command containing both the parsed command and the exact submitted text. Reuse this ordered list for canvas replay and History instead of maintaining independently mutable copies. Include FC, BC, LINEV, LINEH, RECT, CLEAR, and TYPE; exclude HELP, EXIT, parse failures, menu operations, and previews. Preserve typed case, spaces, colons, and Unicode payloads. Mouse-generated records use canonical text in the existing command grammar.
- History displays commands chronologically, wraps complete scalars, and initially shows the newest entries. Preserve its position when switching pages; keep it at the newest end when new commands arrive only if it was already there. Clamp the scroll position after resize. Vertical wheel scrolling over History moves three visual rows per 120 units, accumulating partial deltas; positive delta moves toward older entries. Horizontal wheel and clicks on history rows have no action.

### Shapes menu and drawing

- List exactly ten choices: LINEV THIN/THICK/DOUBLE, LINEH THIN/THICK/DOUBLE, and RECT THIN/THICK/DOUBLE/ROUND. Use this order; initially highlight the first choice and remember the last accepted choice afterward. Up/Down clamps at the ends and keeps the highlighted item visible in a short menu. Enter or a left click accepts. Escape dismisses; TAB closes it and advances navigation. Header clicks take precedence over outside-menu dismissal: Canvas/History closes the menu and activates that page; clicking Shapes again closes the menu and restores its underlying page. Other outside left clicks dismiss and are consumed. Consume the selecting gesture so it cannot also start a canvas drag.
- Accepting a shape activates Canvas and arms one drawing operation. Retain the draft, change only its text to `808080`, and hide its cursor while armed or dragging. Ignore text editing and submission until the operation finishes or is canceled.
- Start a drag only on a left press inside the paper. Treat a left `MouseDoubleClick` as the same press transition, because both production backends replace the second down event with it. Other buttons must not activate controls, start/end a drag, or dismiss overlays.
- Store the anchor and current endpoint in logical paper coordinates. Clamp the endpoint to current paper bounds on both preview movement and release, so the preview at the release coordinate matches the committed geometry. RECT normalizes both axes; LINEV keeps the anchor x and normalizes y; LINEH keeps the anchor y and normalizes x. Endpoints are inclusive. One-cell lines are valid; rectangles require different x and y endpoints. Releasing a degenerate rectangle adds no command and stays armed for another attempt.
- Derive each frame by replaying committed commands, then drawing the current preview with the effective FC/BC state. The preview uses the same drawing helpers and clipping as a committed command. It must neither grow history nor leave old preview pixels, even where its arms merge with earlier lines or it overwrites wide characters.
- A valid left release commits exactly one canonical command and restores the draft's normal text/cursor. A release outside paper but still reported inside the terminal clamps the endpoint to the paper. Ignore duplicate releases after completion. Escape or header/Tab navigation cancels armed/dragging state, including clicking Shapes to open a replacement menu; resize also cancels it before rebuilding layout. All cancellation restores the draft without adding history.
- Native pointer capture outside the terminal is not guaranteed. If a later mouse movement reports the left button is no longer down during an active drag, cancel the preview without committing and restore normal input. Escape remains an available cancellation route when no release or movement is reported.
- Existing HELP/error information is modal and takes precedence over every other interaction. Only Enter dismisses it; Tab, Escape, arrows, clicks, wheel, and ordinary text have no action. Keep HELP's concise command list and EXIT as the only application-controlled quit command. Clear pending UTF-16 assembly state at transitions that disable text input so discarded units cannot join later input.

# TEST [CONFIRMED]

The final MiniHTTP native RPT run also exposed a renderer-takeover failure: `GuiRemoteEventFilter::ProcessResponses` reported outstanding response IDs. `GuiRemoteProtocolCoreChannel::Submit` checked renderer identity only before `BatchWrite`; concurrent admission can detach that renderer while the batch is delivering responses, causing `OnRead` to discard them while `Submit` still reports success. CDB confirmed the deterministic channel regression reached the same assertion with `disconnected == false`. Revalidate renderer identity and the transport guard after the batch, and clear both outstanding IDs and buffered responses when it is cancelled. Regressions cover detachment, changed transport admission, and a successful subsequent response without stale results. A paused live CDB run completed takeover, indicating that the live trigger is timing-sensitive.

The Windows HTTP regression uses the real Windows server and portable HTTP client to return three messages from one callback. It exercises both an already registered poll and a poll started after the inline response. Before the fix, CDB confirmed only the existing-poll case stalled. After the fix, both cases receive `0` inline and `1`, `2` through successive polls, without a recoverable error. Live CDB evidence independently linked that queue state to the renderer-replacement stall.

Regression coverage will exercise shared field defaults and key values, production input conversion and ordered callbacks, playground navigation/history/drag previews, downstream Alt/bracket propagation, generated consumers, and the required Windows live verification matrices. Success requires passing relevant unit tests without Debug leaks, reproducible generated output, and recorded real-terminal/renderer evidence. Unavailable Linux/macOS hosts will remain explicitly pending.

## No.1 Shared input declarations, production decoders, and semantic playground state

The header regression compiles with Debug x64 (zero warnings/errors) and fails under CDB at `backend->renderedBuffer[1].GetChar32() == U'C'`. Existing TUI tests preceding it pass. Source inspection confirms that Windows `GetKeyInfo` omits the virtual key and only character events expand repetitions, while POSIX consumes CSI keys without callbacks and can block despite later buffered input.

Move the complete shared declaration set with comments into `Source/TUI/TUITypes.h`. Add safe defaults and correct bracket aliases. Keep Windows native record conversion in a stateful internal decoder, and extract the POSIX byte decoder into platform-neutral internal code so Windows tests can exercise the exact production algorithm. Preserve owner-thread lifecycle and native character units.

Represent playground navigation, selected shape, drag coordinates, draft, and ordered command/text records as semantic state. Derive layout and frames for replay, preview, history, and hit testing. Keep modal information authoritative. Then propagate shared ownership, mouse Alt and bracket corrections through GacUI/GacJS, run the required generators and downstream checks, and publish a matching release.

Implemented the shared header and project inventory; backend conversion and decoder regression seams; playground header/menu/history/drag implementation and exact frame tests; GacUI Alt/bracket propagation and generated protocol/reflection; GacJS key-enum generation and renderer tests; and specification/SOP updates.
